subject: planet Earth
title: What If the Earth Were Hollow?

scenes.text: What if the Earth were hollow? You couldn't live inside, and not because of the dark.
Step inside a hollow shell and gravity pulls from every direction at once. It cancels out. You'd float.
The shell itself wouldn't last. Just 30 kilometers down, rock is squeezed several times harder than granite can stand.
A hollow planet's crust would crumble inward within moments, under its own weight.
In 1936, Inge Lehmann read earthquake waves and found the opposite: a solid core about 2,400 kilometers wide.
Earth is twice as dense as the rock you stand on. The middle isn't empty. It's the heaviest part.

description:
What if the Earth were hollow? By Newton's shell theorem, gravity cancels everywhere inside a hollow sphere, so you would float, and no rock is strong enough to hold up a planet-sized shell: at about 30 km depth the pressure already exceeds granite's strength several times over.
Inge Lehmann's 1936 study of earthquake waves revealed a solid inner core; Earth's average density (5.5 g/cm3) is about twice that of surface rock.
